findings.issue: `(… as PropertyDeclarationSyntax).Identifier` has no null-conditional. For a metadata property, FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() is null, so `.Identifier` throws NullReferenceException. This replaces the original IndexOutOfRange crash and does not return null as the doc comment and C10 claim. The same happens for a source property that is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, such as a record positional parameter.

The wrapper drops every diagnostic that has no in-compilation source location. That includes the existing `Diagnostic.Create(..., null, ...)` cases and diagnostics located in other trees, not only the metadata ones. It is a broad filter, not a narrow fix. It can silently suppress safety-relevant diagnostics for source types, which contradicts NF1, S1, C4 and C5, and it makes C8 an unproven justification.

`FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()` yields a null location for metadata members. The diagnostic is then dropped by the filter, so metadata members never report MemberNeedsKey. Diagnostics for members of a referenced type are lost without any option to enable them.

The documentation claims that diagnostics for referenced types are reported by the defining assembly. That is not guaranteed: the defining assembly may not run the analyzer, or may be a NuGet package built without it. The claim over-claims behaviour (NF2). The wording 'any problem must be fixed there' is also misleading.

The doc states that unattributed members in referenced types are reported by the defining project. This is unverified and over-claims, because the defining project may never have been analyzed. It also changes the documented scope of MsgPack004.

The test name and the comment for the unkeyed-member case assert that no diagnostic is produced. They do not verify that the diagnostic is reported anywhere else. The tests also cover only the property path; fields, the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path, and class<T> or non-generic struct from metadata (F3 regressions) are not tested. The metadata-reference tests therefore do not support C3.
